correctness.rationale: The greedy mex sequence strictly increases: all smaller positive values were already represented, and the previous mex becomes available as a singleton. For the legal-subset recurrence, if the top index n is selected, the only possible selection among the preceding k positions is n-k+c. With that position selected, any previous compatible index is at most n-2(k-c)<n-k, so no extra restriction from n remains. The admissible k-bit transfer matrix is primitive by paths through the all-zero word and its self-loop; the recurrence then identifies its Perron rate with the stated rho. The positive eventual greedy recurrence similarly gives growth rate lambda via its irreducible companion with a self-loop. At lambda, the count polynomial is -(lambda-1)lambda^c<0, and its factorized level function increases strictly above one. To check the truncation, choose fixed L so that lambda^(1-L)/(lambda-1)<1. Eventually even the sum of all terms through index n-L is below a_n, while no index n or later can occur. Counting each legal subset separately gives bounds d_(n-L) and d_(n-1) before division by a_n. For the second limit, w=k(lambda-1) satisfies w+log w=log k+O(w^2/k), with w tending to infinity and w=O(log k); thus w=W(k)+o(1). Uniformly on [lambda,lambda+2(lambda-1)/k] the derivative of the count polynomial is asymptotic to k. Its negative value at lambda is asymptotic to -(lambda-1); this gives a sign change on the interval and rho-lambda asymptotic to (lambda-1)/k. The example ratio independently evaluates to 1.011434032776249 by root bisection. This establishes exponential comparison, not a limiting prefactor; the eventual greedy recurrence is still a hypothesis outside the cited proved range. The uploaded finite verification was inspected, not executed.
